candidates.label: A
candidates.notes: All words, readings and line numbers (8–46) are correct and present. The header is not marked as a heading, and the ＊影響を及ぼす / ＊心に芽生える sub-entries are flattened to the same level as main entries. Column break is only a blank line.

candidates.label: B
candidates.notes: All line numbers (8, 9, 10 … 46) are omitted. Readings are rewritten as inline per-kanji furigana, e.g. 効(き)く and 見(み)た目(め), where the source has the word followed by the full reading in parentheses. The reading for まとめる（まとめる） is dropped. Sub-entries are nested correctly.

candidates.label: C
candidates.notes: Text, readings and line numbers are all accurate and complete. Sub-entries are indented with a full-width space. However, entries are plain lines with no list markup or hard breaks, so they would collapse into one paragraph when rendered as markdown.

candidates.label: D
candidates.notes: Complete and accurate, with all line numbers, words and readings. Has a heading, bulleted entries, properly nested ＊ sub-entries, and a rule separating the two columns. The most faithful to the page layout.

candidates.label: E
candidates.notes: All line numbers are omitted. Reading format is inconsistent: な-adjectives and する-verbs are rewritten inline, e.g. 立派(りっぱ)な and 影響(えいきょう)する, while other entries keep the original trailing parentheses. Keeps まとめる（まとめる） and nests sub-entries correctly. The bold on 017 is harmless.

rationale: D, A and C all transcribe every word, reading and line number correctly, so they are separated by formatting: D has heading, bullets, nested sub-entries and a column separator; A has clean bullets but flattens sub-entries and lacks a heading; C would run together when rendered. E and B both drop all line numbers and restructure the readings. E ranks above B because it keeps the original parenthetical form for most entries and retains まとめる（まとめる）, whereas B converts everything to per-kanji furigana and drops that reading.
